questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting non-chord tones in a melody
questions.stem: In a historical case, explain why non-chord tones are counted in a melody analysis.

answer.exemplar: Counting non-chord tones reveals the melodic embellishment layered over the harmony, distinguishing structural pitches from decorative ones.

questions.explanation: The count separates structural chord tones from decorative non-chord tones. That reveals the melody's embellishment.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The submediant and its effect on a cadence
questions.stem: In a historical case, explain why a cadence to vi is called deceptive.

answer.exemplar: The listener expects resolution to tonic, but the harmony moves to the submediant instead, deceiving that expectation and creating an open, surprising close.

questions.explanation: The expected tonic resolution is replaced by submediant. That deception creates an open, surprising close.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The span a passing tone bridges
questions.stem: In a historical case, a diatonic passing tone bridges a

options.text: Fifth between two chord tones
Half step between two chord tones
Third between two chord tones
Whole step between two chord tones

questions.explanation: A diatonic passing tone fills a whole-step gap. Chromatic passing tones handle half steps, but the standard diatonic span is a whole step.
